# 01. First program

**Tier:** Core. **Why you'd use this:** You want a tiny program that prints a greeting, and you need to know where to look when the first error appears. A notebook also keeps names between cells, which helps when you experiment and confuses you when you forget what already ran.

**After this lesson you can:** run a short `.py` file and read what `print` writes; find the problem on the last line of an error; say what a notebook remembers between cells, and what a fresh run of a file forgets.
About 20 minutes. **Uses:** nothing yet

# 02. How practice works

**Tier:** Core. **Why you'd use this:** Every practice notebook in this course works the same way. You replace a stub, run checks, and read a ✓ or an error. Knowing that loop once saves you from fighting the harness on every later topic.

**After this lesson you can:** replace `raise NotImplementedError` and run a check; tell `return` from `print` when a check reads a value; open a hint only after you have tried.
About 20 minutes. **Uses:** [First program](01-first-program-lesson.ipynb)

## Quick review

1. Where do you look first in an error message?
2. Does a fresh run of a `.py` file remember names from the last run?

<details><summary>Answers</summary>

The last line names the problem. A fresh run of a file starts empty; a notebook keeps names until you restart the kernel.
</details>
